::: {#exm-gru}

#### Parameters of `nn.GRU` and `nn.LSTM`

```{python}
#| code-fold: show
def n_params(net):
    return sum(p.numel() for p in net.parameters())


gru_count = n_params(nn.GRU(1, 32))
lstm_count = n_params(nn.LSTM(1, 32))
print(gru_count, lstm_count)
```

A [GRU](#def-gru) layer has three blocks of weights,
for $\vecf{z}_t$, $\vecf{r}_t$ and $\vecf{u}_t$,
where an [LSTM](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/cnn-rnn.html#def-lstm) layer has four.
PyTorch gives each block two bias vectors,
one added to $\matr{W} \vx_t$ and one to $\matr{U} \vhidval_{t-1}$ [@pytorch_gru].
So `nn.GRU(1, 32)` has $3 \times 32 \times (1 + 32 + 2) = `r py$gru_count`$ [parameters](https://morrison-lab.github.io/lds/chapters/big-ideas.html#def-parameter),
and `nn.LSTM(1, 32)` has $4 \times 32 \times (1 + 32 + 2) = `r py$lstm_count`$.

:::
